new_signals.name: samp_chk
new_signals.comment_in_source: sample-phase qualifier, reused for ordinary bit-sample bookkeeping

secret_signal_leaked.name: cnt
secret_signal_leaked.role_in_clean_design: free-running 16-bit clock-divider counter used internally to generate the SCL/SDA bit timing (commented in the clean source as "clock divider counter (synthesis)"); not an architectural secret in the conventional sense, but an internal accumulator with no legitimate path to any host-visible register in the clean design

leak_destination.name: dout
leak_destination.role_in_clean_design: single-bit SDA sample register; shifted, 8 bits at a time, into the byte controller's RXR (receive data register), which is the host-visible Wishbone register a software driver reads to get the last I2C-read byte

inputs_used.name: cmd
inputs_used.description: 4-bit command input from the byte controller; 4'b1000 is the existing I2C_CMD_READ encoding (already `defined in the source)

inputs_used.name: slave_adr
inputs_used.description: existing 8-bit register in i2c_master_bit_ctrl that passively snoops any START+8-bits sequence observed on the bus (used by the design's own multi-master slave-mode logic); it is NOT restricted to addresses this core owns, so it also captures the core's own master-mode transactions

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: the read-phase (RW=1) I2C address byte for 7-bit slave address 0x35, i.e. {7'b0110101, 1'b1} = 8'b01101011 = 0x6b

payload.description: on every rising edge of the filtered/synchronized SCL (sSCL & ~dSCL), if the trigger condition holds, dout is loaded from the internal counter's bit 0 instead of the real sampled SDA line; otherwise behavior is identical to the clean design

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone + I2C top-level ports of i2c_master_top (no internal/hierarchical probing)
procedure: issue a WRITE transaction addressed at 7-bit SADR=0x35 (any data byte)
issue a repeated-START READ transaction addressed at the same SADR=0x35; this snoops the read-phase address byte 0x6b into slave_adr
the entire following 8-bit RXR data read (plus its trailing host-ACK bit sample) occurs while slave_adr==8'h6b and cmd==READ, so every dout sample for that byte is corrupted to cnt[0]

read back RXR: for a fixed PRER (fixed clock-divider period), cnt happens to equal the same value at every SCL rising edge within one bit period, so the leaked byte is deterministically 8'h00 in this testbench; a different PRER value, a different starting phase, or any downstream consumer sampling RXR across multiple reads with varying bus timing would observe the counter's live value rather than a constant

one_shot_or_persistent: re-arms every time the design re-enters the trigger condition (not a one-shot latch); fires on every bit sampled while cmd==READ and slave_adr==8'h6b, and is fully inactive the instant either condition stops holding

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of all three design files, top-module chip area 9975.8176 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: golden testbench only ever drives SADR=0x10, which produces slave_adr values 0x20/0x21 during READ commands -- confirmed via an instrumented probe build -- never 0x6b, so the trigger never activates

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone/I2C ports
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: SADR=0x10 near-miss (match), SADR=0x35 full read transaction (TRIGGER, infected read back 0x00 leaked vs clean's correct 0x77), SADR=0x35 write-only near-miss with no READ command issued (match) -- 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger mismatch

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, samp_chk, is named and commented as ordinary bit-sample bookkeeping with no trigger/trojan/leak terminology; the diff against the clean file is a 2-line wire declaration/comment and a one-line change to the existing dout-generation always block -- port list, parameters, and the module's instantiation inside i2c_master_byte_ctrl are all untouched; both inputs to the trigger (cmd, slave_adr) are pre-existing signals already computed by the module for its own slave-mode/multi-master logic, so no new hierarchical or cross-module reference is introduced
